lead: Monitoring in labour follows the fetus, the progress and the mother. The partogram shows slow labour early, and CTG looks for fetal hypoxia in high-risk labour. Slow progress must be sorted into weak contractions, which are treated, and obstruction, which needs a caesarean.
f: Opened in the active phase at 4 cm, starting on the alert line · Alert line: 1 cm/h from 4 cm · Action line: 4 h to the right · Crossing the alert line in a health centre: refer · Crossing the action line: full review of the 3 Ps · Fetus: FHR every 30 min (110–160), liquor (I, C, M, B, A), moulding 0 to +3 · Progress: cervix (X) every 4 h, descent in fifths, contractions every 30 min · Mother: pulse 30 min, BP 4 h, temperature 2 h, urine

sc: Liquor B with maternal tachycardia → Suspect abruption
tr: Number of boxes = frequency, shading = duration; fewer than 3 in 10 min or under 40 s is inefficient

f: Contractions 3–5 in 10 min; over 5 = tachysystole · Baseline 110–160 bpm · Variability 5–25 bpm · Accelerations (≥ 15 bpm for 15 s) = healthy fetus · Decelerations: early (head compression), late (placental hypoxia), variable (cord), prolonged over 3 min · CTG is sensitive, not specific: in low-risk women it only raises caesareans

sc: Dip after the peak of every contraction, pre-eclampsia → Late decelerations: placental insufficiency
Flat trace 30 min, then accelerations return → Fetal sleep: normal

f: Suspicious: baseline 100–109 or 161–180, variability under 5 for 30–50 min, uncomplicated variable decelerations · Pathological: baseline under 100 or over 180, variability under 5 for over 50 min, sinusoidal, repeated late decelerations, one over 3 min · Normal = all normal; suspicious = one suspicious; pathological = one pathological or two suspicious · FHR over 160: fever, chorioamnionitis, hypoxia · Under 100: cord prolapse, abruption, rupture, epidural hypotension · Sinusoidal: severe fetal anaemia

First stage: under 2 cm in 4 h in the active phase, or crossing the action line · Second stage: over 2 h primi (3 h epidural), over 1 h multi (2 h epidural) · Prolonged labour: over 18 h · Causes: power (commonest, mainly primi), passenger (OP, malpresentation, macrosomia), passage (CPD) · Weak contractions, no CPD, fetus well: ARM + oxytocin, VE in 2 h · Tired and dry: fluids and analgesia · Slow progress in a multipara = obstruction until proved otherwise

sc: Primi, 6 cm for 4 h, 2 weak contractions → ARM + oxytocin

f: No descent despite good contractions from a mechanical block: CPD, brow, mento-posterior face, shoulder, hydrocephalus, locked twins · Exhausted, dry, ketotic, febrile · Bandl's ring, head 3/5 or more at full dilatation, moulding +3, caput, swollen cervix, haematuria · Complications: uterine rupture (multi), VVF/RVF (primi), sepsis, PPH, foot drop, fetal death · Resuscitate, antibiotics, catheter → caesarean even if the fetus is dead · Catheter 14 days after birth to prevent fistula

tr: Never give oxytocin in obstructed labour
sc: Grand multipara, obstructed labour, given oxytocin → Uterine rupture
Leaking urine 10 days after a long labour → Vesicovaginal fistula

f: Pathological CTG; thick meconium; FHR under 100 or over 160; late decelerations · Fetal scalp pH: 7.25 or more normal; 7.21–7.24 repeat in 30 min; 7.20 or less: deliver · Intrauterine resuscitation: left lateral, stop oxytocin, IV fluids, treat hypotension, terbutaline 0.25 mg SC for hyperstimulation, VE for cord prolapse · Deliver: first stage → emergency CS; second stage → instrumental

sc: Multi fully dilated 1 h, late decelerations, head 0/5, OA → Ventouse or forceps
